_readme: EXPERIMENTAL (PRD 14.3): each speaker's radio chatter, the 'wawawa' under a comms line. Heard in a run when the player turns Character voices on in the pause menu (default off), and on the sound test page (/tools/sound-test/ under npm run dev). A voice strings its syllables in random order: pitchHz is the voice's middle pitch (each syllable's own frequency slot is ignored; syllableNames only labels them on the page), pitchRangeSemitones is how far a syllable wanders either way, phraseEndSemitones bends the last syllable of a phrase (negative falls like a statement, positive rises like a question), syllablesPerPhrase is [fewest, most], and the two gaps are in seconds. A syllable is a ZzFX array or the Sound Designer's pasted text, as in sounds.json, under 0.25 s long. The vowel comes from the last slot, the filter: a negative number is a low-pass whose resonance sounds like a vowel (about -500 oo, -800 oh, -1200 ah, -1800 eh, -2500 ee). Slide (slot 8) bends a syllable by slide × 500 Hz per second: negative sounds like 'wa'. Noise (slot 13) adds rasp or breath, bitCrush (slot 15) adds grit. radio is the band every voice goes through (lowCutHz, highCutHz), its saturation (drive, 0 clean to 1), and every voice's loudness against the effects (level, 0 to 1: turn the whole cast up or down here, and a single speaker with their syllables' volumes). Every voice here is a PLACEHOLDER first pass by the engineer, for the owner to tune.
